evals.prompt: We are about to ship a fine-tuned model and nobody can tell me whether it was ever evaluated. Can you find out?
evals.expected_output: The answer reports what it actually found: whether any SageMaker evaluation or benchmark job ran against this model, when, and with what result. Where nothing is found it says so plainly and states the shipping risk, rather than describing how evaluation could be done. It separates what read-only APIs confirmed from what it cannot see.
assertions: The response reports actual findings about whether an evaluation job ran, rather than only explaining how to evaluate
The response states the risk of shipping without evaluation if none is found
The response separates what it verified from what it could not determine
The response names the specific job or resource it inspected

assertions.text: At least one finding carries a SM-EVAL check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed

evals.prompt: Our Nova evaluation recipe ran as a SageMaker job against our fine-tuned model and failed. Why?
evals.expected_output: The answer names the job's failure reason and the container logs as the authoritative sources, then the common causes for a recipe-based evaluation: the recipe and its parameters, the benchmark dataset location and format, the execution role's access to the model artifact and the dataset including any KMS key, and instance capacity or quota. It reports what it found.
assertions: The response names the job failure reason and logs as the first sources to read
The response lists concrete candidate causes specific to a recipe-based evaluation
The response addresses the execution role's access to the model artifact and dataset
The response reports actual findings rather than only possibilities

assertions.text: At least one finding carries a SM-EVAL check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed

assertions: The response identifies the lack of durably retained structured results as the problem
The response explains why scores held only in job logs cannot support comparison
The response prescribes a concrete persistence mechanism keyed to the model version

evals.prompt: Our LLM-as-judge evaluation on SageMaker gives scores that swing a lot between runs on the same model.
evals.expected_output: The answer attributes the variance to the judge configuration and sample size: judge sampling parameters, a rubric that permits interpretation, and too few examples per run. It prescribes fixing the judge's decoding parameters, tightening the rubric, and increasing the sample so the aggregate is stable.
assertions: The response attributes the variance to the judge configuration or sample size rather than to the model under test
The response prescribes fixing the judge's sampling parameters
The response addresses the sample size or statistical stability of the aggregate

evals.prompt: Our fine-tuned model scores far better on our benchmark than it does with users. We fine-tuned on data from the same source as the benchmark.
evals.expected_output: The answer names train/test contamination as the likely explanation, explains that overlap between fine-tuning data and the benchmark inflates scores without improving generalisation, and prescribes a held-out set disjoint from the training data plus a check for overlap.
assertions: The response identifies contamination or overlap between the fine-tuning data and the benchmark as the cause
The response explains why that inflates the score without improving real performance
The response prescribes a disjoint held-out set and an overlap check
